newsitem.title: UK: Music company EMI optimistic despite earnings drop.
newsitem.headline: Music company EMI optimistic despite earnings drop.

text.p: EMI, one of the world's top five music companies, said Tuesday that its pre-tax profits fell by 6 percent in the last three quarters of 1996, but it expected strong sales in the current quarter to propel it to modest profit growth this year.

EMI -- with artists ranging from The Beatles to newcomers The Spice Girls -- said its profit before tax and exceptional items fell to 293.3 million pounds ($480 million) in the nine months ended Dec. 31.
The fall, however, would have been less than 1 percent at constant exchange rates but the strength of the pound sterling wiped 16 million pounds ($26.2 million) off operating profit in the period.

Finance Director Simon Duffy said that EMI still expected to meet analysts' forecasts for full year pre-tax profitsbetween 380 million and 400 million pounds ($622 million and $655 million), excluding exceptional gains. He was confident of achieving that target despite currency factors.
EMI had 1996 pre-tax profit of 367 million pounds ($601 million).
Duffy noted that recent albums from two of its bands, Blur and Mansun, had entered the British charts at number one.

The company is also expecting continuing high sales from The Spice Girls, whose debut album has sold more than 7 million copies worldwide, he said. The quintet, whose debut single has topped the U.S. charts, picked up two top honours at the annual British pop awards Monday night.
EMI, PolyGram NV , Bertelsmann , Sony Music and Warner dominate the music industry worldwide, accounting for more than two thirds of sales.
The industry has expanded rapidly in recent years and the retail market has grown to a value of some $40 billion. However, growth slowed to around 3 percent last year.
EMI said the retail market remained tough in the United States and also noted tough economic conditions in major European markets such as France and Germany.
However, it said that overall it had great confidence in the health of the market in the coming years, pointing to robust growth in South America, Southeast Asia and Eastern Europe.
